# Rollback Drill Decision: Atlas Rehearsals

**Date:** 2026-07-02
**Participants:** Quinton Fairweather (CTO)

Quinton: "Atlas rollback rehearsals run monthly from now on. A rollback
we have not rehearsed is a rollback we do not actually have."

Key decisions:
- **Cadence**: monthly Atlas rollback rehearsals
- **Owner**: Quinton Fairweather

positions.frame: what makes a rollback capability real — is an unrehearsed rollback procedure actually possessed, and does that justify a fixed recurring cadence set by decree?
positions.why: src-1 issues the monthly directive, src-2 supplies the aphoristic justification equating unrehearsed with nonexistent capability, and src-3 restates the cadence as a structural spec field — all three share the authority-ranking, competence/conservation-value read that a recurring rehearsal rhythm is being both mandated and justified as constitutive of actually having the capability, not merely reducing risk around it.

placements.why: This envelope establishes a recurring, owned operational discipline (monthly rollback rehearsal cadence) justified by a claim about what makes a capability real. Nothing in the supplied strata (currently empty) covers organizational-reliability-practice categories, and the content is squarely about instituting and owning a maintenance discipline rather than a strategy, product, or proof-point concern — so a new top-level category is warranted rather than forcing this under an unrelated existing tier.
placements.title: operational readiness as a maintained practice, not a static state
placements.frame: does this content name a recurring organizational discipline — a rehearsed, owned, cadenced practice — that keeps a system's emergency capabilities actually usable, as distinct from one-off engineering or product work?

placements.title: rehearsed capability as the only capability that actually exists
placements.frame: when a recurring rehearsal cadence is mandated and owned, is the claim being tested whether a capability that has not been practiced can be said to exist at all — and does the cadence-plus-ownership structure itself constitute the proof?
placements.why: src-1 and src-3 institute a monthly rollback-rehearsal cadence, src-2 supplies the constitutive claim that an unrehearsed rollback is not actually possessed, and src-4 assigns the named owner who carries the practice forward. Together these are not a one-time fact but a recurring, generalizable theme — that a capability's reality is contingent on its being practiced under an accountable owner — which future envelopes about other rehearsal or readiness decisions would plausibly keep feeding. No existing narrative leaf exists yet in this graph to hold it, so this is a foundational mint rather than a reuse.
